property_summary: For any non-owner caller, invoking owned() must transfer ownership to that caller (owner == msg.sender after the call); the mutant leaves owner unchanged, so for some caller owner differs.

For any caller x, a call to owned() must either revert (because x is not the owner) or, if it succeeds, make the owner equal x; the mutant's emptied owned() breaks this because whenever the call succeeds the owner may remain different from the caller.

For any address, a call to owned() either reverts (caller is not owner) or, if it succeeds, sets owner to the caller; the mutant's emptied owned() leaves owner unchanged after a successful call, so for the owner-caller scenario the post-state ownership identity rule diverges.

For every caller, a call to owned() must either revert (caller is not the current owner) or, if it succeeds, set the owner to the caller (owner == msg.sender after the call); the mutant's emptied owned() makes successful calls leave the owner unchanged, so for a successful call from the current owner the post-call ownership rule diverges in the mutated contract.

For any caller, a call to owned() must either revert (caller is not the current owner) or, if it succeeds, leave the owner equal to the caller; the emptied mutant still succeeds for the owner but we distinguish it by checking the post-call ownership identity via the try/catch success flag paired with c.owner().
Calling owned() as the current owner never changes or abandons ownership; the owner address remains the same nonzero address afterwards.

property_summary: After burning some amount, totalSupply must equal the supply before the burn minus the burned amount (for any amounts).
Calling owned() from any account never reverts on the original contract, but always reverts for a non-owner under the inverted-modifier mutant.
Burning tokens must decrease totalSupply by exactly the burned amount.
Burning reduces totalSupply by exactly the amount removed from the burner's balance, so the difference totalSupply - balanceOf(burner) is invariant across a burn.
An account that is the current owner of C can always successfully call owned(); under the inverted-modifier mutant the owner is barred and the call reverts.
